A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 19-page versions of the same LED paper, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–19 are unchanged; the differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, decoding comparisons, ablations, entropy analyses, and a reasoning case study in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1 and 4 and ablations in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C retain identical top-k filtering, cumulative aggregation, entropy selection, exploration/exploitation switching, and DeepThink-only decoding procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024/2025, GPQA-Diamond, and LiveCodeBench v5. The represented tasks, domains, and additional test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: CoT, DoLa, SoftThinking, and SoftThinking-Gumbel remain the evaluated comparators in the corresponding benchmark comparisons, including Tables 1 and 4. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices B.3 and D retain the same models, sample sizes, metrics, generation limits, prompts, verification procedures, and sampling configurations.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, exploration-depth analysis in Figure 7, case study in Figure 6, and top-k/top-p comparison in Table 5 are identical.

E5.justification: Both describe pass@1 averaged over 16 runs and specify random seed 0. Repeated-run information, statistical estimation procedures, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings in Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–8 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains LED's Qwen3-4B-Thinking overall pass@1/pass@16 values of 79.32/89.86.

T1.justification: The method equations, entropy definitions, and Appendix B's GRPO reasoning are identical. The qualification that the mechanistic explanation is not a formal convergence proof is also retained.

C1.justification: The claims about exploration collapse, intermediate-layer entropy, training-free LED, and average improvements of 0.61/1.03 percentage points remain unchanged. Added bold emphasis does not alter their meaning or scope.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations, ablation explanations, and applicability qualifications remain identical, including Appendix D.2's discussion of failure to improve QwQ-32B's overall pass@16.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the Xiaomi-Research/LED project link marked 'coming soon' with AlbertTan404/Latent-Exploration-Decoding and removes that qualification. This changes access information; implementation code, hardware, and hyperparameter documentation remain unchanged. The PDFs do not verify repository availability or contents.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix A's related-work discussion are identical, including LED's positioning relative to DoLa and soft decoding methods. The project-link update is not a change to cited prior research.

P1.justification: Page 1 updates the preprint date, arXiv version/date text, and project-page wording. The scientific prose, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds bold emphasis to the abstract's existing performance claim and changes its line wrapping around the revised link. All figures, tables, and page layouts after page 1 are identical.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves documented access guidance by replacing the project reference marked 'coming soon' with an updated repository link. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged, so the benefit is limited to documentation; actual repository availability and contents cannot be established from the PDFs.
